slots_and_copies.name: slot_0
slots_and_copies.selection_rule: Only one header copy observed in the 512-byte image (signature at 0x00, no mirrored copy in 0x10-0x1FF). No backup selection rule is reconstructable; on integrity failure at offset 0x08 the probe reverted to a blank save and rewrote it, so failure handling is reject-and-reinitialize.

checksums.name: header_sum8_complement
checksums.formula_detail: stored = (~(sum of covered bytes)) & 0xFF = 0xFF - (sum & 0xFF); equivalently (sum + stored) & 0xFF == 0xFF. Minimal proven cover is 0x00-0x0F excluding the stored byte at 0x08 (byte 0x0E is proven covered by the cap-00 -> cap-01 differential: 0x0E +1 drives stored 0xEC -> 0xEB). A whole-image cover 0x00-0x1FF excluding 0x08 yields identical values because 0x10-0x1FF is 0x00 fill and cannot be excluded. Ruled out on both samples: negation -sum8 (0xED/0xEC), xor8 (0x0D/0x0C), CRC-16/MODBUS (0x5D48/0xCD49). Implementing routine not present in the 201 decompiled functions.

io_driver_functions.notes: EEPROM block read: builds MSB-first read bitstream (address bits + opcode 11), DMA3 via 0x08037540 to/from 0x0D000000 (addr_bits+3 then 0x44 halfwords), repacks 64 bits into 4x u16 at param_2+6..+0. One 8-byte block per call. Address rejected unless < *(u16 *)(cfg+4); address-bit count from *(u8 *)(cfg+8). No callers in callgraph (indirect tails unrecovered).

EEPROM block write: serializes 4x u16 (64 bits) + address bits + start/opcode 01, DMA3 via 0x08037540 to 0x0D000000 (addr_bits+0x43 halfwords), then 0x08037474, busy-polls EEPROM line uRam0d000000 bit0 and status byte until write cycle ends, then 0x080374fc. One 8-byte block per call. No callers in callgraph (indirect tails unrecovered).

DMA3 transfer primitive used for both directions: programs source/destination shadow registers and control word param_3 & 0xFFFF | 0x80000000, polls CNT high halfword bit15 until clear. Register layout matches DMA3 (0x040000D4 base) by order; literal addresses unresolved in export.

Interrupt/DMA channel setup helper called by the EEPROM write path before the busy-poll: sets channel mask (8 << channel), stores 3 halfwords from argument into a shadow struct, sets active flag. Transport support only; touches no save-image fields.
Interrupt/DMA teardown helper called at the end of the EEPROM write path: clears the halfword pair set up by 0x08037474, clears channel bit, restores saved handler word. Transport support only.

fields.name: magic_signature
fields.update_mechanism: Occupies EEPROM block 0; transported as one 8-byte block by 0x08037670 (write) / 0x080375c0 (read). The routine that writes/compares the literal was not found in the 201 decompiled functions (zero hits for Q00ABGPH/Q00/0x51).
fields.evidence: Byte-identical in both real .sav captures; load-time comparison unproven in code. Mutation tests 2-3 in the report isolate whether it is checked.

fields.name: header_checksum
fields.update_mechanism: Recomputed as (~sum8 of covered bytes) & 0xFF whenever a covered byte changes (cap-00 -> cap-01: byte 0x0E +1, checksum -1). Byte 0 of EEPROM block 1, transported by 0x08037670/0x080375c0. Computing routine not in corpus.
fields.evidence: Matches ~sum8 on both captures under minimal cover [0,16) excl 8 (0xEC, 0xEB) and under whole-image cover; -sum8, xor8 and CRC-16/MODBUS ruled out. Cold-reload probe: mutating offset 0x08 reverted the save to blank and rewrote it (integrity_check_confirmed).

fields.name: header_pad_09_0d
fields.update_mechanism: Inside the proven checksum cover and EEPROM block 1; always zero in this corpus. Possibly reserved header bytes or high bytes of wider fields.
fields.evidence: Zero in both captures; no code reference located.

fields.name: counter_u16_at_0e
fields.update_mechanism: Incremented by 1 between the two captures, driving the offset-0x08 checksum down by 1. Semantics unknown: write counter, sequence counter, or progress flag. A u8 counter at 0x0E plus a zero byte at 0x0F is equally consistent with observations.
fields.evidence: Only non-checksum byte that changed (0x00 -> 0x01 at 0x0E, 0x0F stays 0x00); inside the proven checksum cover. No writer located in code.

fields.name: tail_fill_10_1ff
fields.update_mechanism: Never written in either capture. Either unused EEPROM space or payload blocks this capture scenario never reached. Whole-image checksum cover cannot be excluded while this region is fill.
fields.evidence: Direct byte scan of both 512-byte files: no non-zero byte at or above 0x10. No second signature or backup copy exists here.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Flip stored checksum 0xEC -> 0xED with no repair
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Save rejected on cold reload; game boots as blank/new save and rewrites the save (replicates the recorded probe behavior).
If the Q00ABGPH signature is compared on load, the save is rejected despite a valid checksum; if it loads, the signature is decorative or unchecked.
Rejection implies all 8 signature bytes are compared; acceptance localizes the compared prefix to fewer than 8 bytes.
A changed continue state, counter, or progression indicates the field's semantics; no visible change indicates a pure write/sequence counter.
Clamp, wrap, or reject behavior distinguishes a counter from bitflags at 0x0E.
Any UI/progress change promotes offset 0x09 from zero pad to a live header field; no change keeps it reserved.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Set 0x00 -> 0x01; try whole-image checksum repair, then [0,16)-only repair
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Discriminates the checksum cover: whole-image repair loading while 16-byte repair is rejected proves the cover extends past 0x0F; both loading means the byte is uncovered or unread.
Acceptance with no gameplay change supports an unused EEPROM tail; rejection would prove the upper half is checksummed/read.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Zero the entire image (blank EEPROM baseline)
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Game boots as a new save; on first save it rewrites at least blocks 0-1. Diffing the rewritten image against cap-00-future-0.sav reveals the true initialized header.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Reset 0x0E 0x01 -> 0x00 while keeping cap-01 checksum 0xEB, no repair
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Rejection confirms byte 0x0E is inside the checksum cover on the load path, not only on the write path.

open_questions: Which routine computes the ~sum8 checksum and compares Q00ABGPH, and which gameplay callers invoke the EEPROM block read/write wrappers (0x080375c0/0x08037670)? Neither exists among the 201 decompiled functions and callgraph indirect tails (254 UNRECOVERED_JUMPTABLE) are unrecovered.

What is the RAM base address (0x02xxxxxx/0x03xxxxxx) and layout of the save struct the block drivers copy to/from? All _DAT_ literals in the export are unresolved and no 0x020/0x030 literal appears in decompiled.c.
Does the checksum cover stop at 0x0F or run over the whole 512-byte image? Indistinguishable while 0x10-0x1FF is 0x00 fill; fuzzing targets at 0x10 and 0x100 discriminate.
What does the u16_le candidate at 0x0E count (write counter, sequence, progress), and what are bytes 0x09-0x0D and 0x0F for?
Are EEPROM blocks at 0x10-0x1FF ever written in longer play, and what fields would they hold?

What are the literal EEPROM config values (block count at cfg+4, address-bit count at cfg+8) stripped with the _DAT_ literal pool? 64 blocks / 6 address bits is inferred from the 512-byte image, not read from code.
Is there any slot/backup redundancy in longer play, or is the single header at block 0-1 the only copy?
